claims.text: A controlled heat treatment using precise cooling and quenching can form coherent nanoprecipitates in a tungsten high-entropy alloy.
The induced coherent nanoprecipitates will be uniformly distributed within the tungsten HEA matrix.
Coherent nanoprecipitates impede dislocation motion in tungsten HEAs at high temperature.
Coherent nanoprecipitates inhibit crack propagation in tungsten HEAs at high temperature.
Impeded dislocation motion increases high-temperature plastic-strain tolerance.
Inhibited crack propagation increases high-temperature fracture toughness.
Nanoprecipitate-containing heat-treated tungsten HEAs will exhibit a statistically significant increase in plastic strain relative to the unperturbed baseline at temperatures above 1000°C.
Nanoprecipitate-containing heat-treated tungsten HEAs will exhibit a statistically significant increase in fracture toughness relative to the unperturbed baseline at temperatures above 1000°C.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply to tungsten HEAs under mechanical loading representative of fusion plasma-facing component operation.
Controlled-atmosphere mechanical testing above 1000°C can simulate fusion plasma-facing component environments.
The initial material is a tungsten HEA with a uniform microstructure and no deliberately induced nanoprecipitates.
The baseline consists of conventionally heat-treated tungsten HEA samples without deliberate nanoprecipitate formation.
The optimal nanoprecipitate size, distribution, and volume fraction are not yet determined.
